findings.title: Migration crashes when no `embed_category` site setting row exists
findings.body: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` assumes at least one row. On the vast majority of sites the `embed_category` setting is unset (no row in site_settings) or doesn't match a category name, so the result set is empty and `[0]` is nil, raising NoMethodError and aborting the migration/deploy. Guard with a presence check before dereferencing. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, which also returns no row when the setting was never persisted.

findings.title: `create_table ... force: true` and raw string interpolation in migration
findings.body: `force: true` issues a DROP TABLE IF EXISTS before creating, so re-running the migration (or running it on a DB where the table already has rows) silently destroys existing embeddable_hosts data. Additionally line 25 interpolates `#{h}` (a value taken from the old site setting) directly into an INSERT string without quoting/escaping, so a host value containing a single quote breaks the SQL (and is an injection vector in a migration). Use `force: false`/no force and bind/quote the value (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

findings.title: before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` is called unconditionally in before_validation. Saving an EmbeddableHost with a nil host (e.g. admin submits an empty host, or `EmbeddableHost.new.save`) raises NoMethodError on nil instead of producing a validation error, resulting in a 500 from the admin controller. Guard with `return if host.blank?`.

findings.title: Case-sensitive host lookup and inconsistent return value
findings.body: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` compares the lowercased stored host against the raw `uri.host`, which is not downcased. A referer like `https://EvilTrout.com` yields host `EvilTrout.com` and never matches the stored `eviltrout.com`, so legitimate embeds are rejected. Downcase the argument. Also `record_for_host` returns `false` on parse failure but `nil`/record otherwise, which is an inconsistent contract for callers such as `TopicEmbed.import`.

findings.title: update/destroy raise 500 on unknown id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can return nil; `save_host(nil)` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` on nil, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of a 404/400. Use `find_by` plus an explicit not-found response, or `find`.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding does nothing
findings.body: `update` only re-serializes the freshly fetched state and ignores the request body, so the client's `saveChanges` action (admin-embedding controller `embedding.update({})`) is a silent no-op. Either implement the update or remove the route/UI action so administrators are not misled into thinking changes were saved.

findings.title: `*_ids` hydration crashes / produces undefined entries
findings.body: The new branch assumes `obj[k]` is an array for any key matching `_ids` and calls `.map` on it; a scalar or null value (common for server payloads) throws a TypeError. Also, when `_lookupSubType` cannot resolve an id (sub-collection missing from the payload), `map` yields `undefined` entries and the original `_ids` key is deleted regardless, so the caller loses the ids and gets a list of undefineds. Guard with `Ember.isArray` and filter out unresolved entries (or keep the ids when nothing resolves, as the singular branch does).

findings.title: Only the first underscore is converted when matching admin models
findings.body: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence (no /g, no regex), so a multi-word admin type such as `embeddable_host_thing` or any future `a_b_c` type will not match the dash-separated entries in ADMIN_MODELS and will be routed to `/` instead of `/admin/`. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')`.

findings.title: No uniqueness validation on host
findings.body: Nothing prevents creating two EmbeddableHost rows with the same host but different categories; `record_for_host` then arbitrarily returns whichever `.first` the DB yields, making the category assignment for imported topics nondeterministic. Add a uniqueness validation (and ideally a unique index).

findings.title: Fabricator file contents swapped
findings.body: `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines only the `:embeddable_host` fabricator while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines the category fabricators. The file names no longer match their contents, which will confuse anyone looking for these definitions; swap the contents back.
